rationale: The agent verified identity correctly using full name and zip via the tool and matched a single user. They retrieved the order, confirmed it was pending, and correctly noted the items. The user asked to change address to an NYC address and modify a laptop that wasn’t in the order; the agent properly checked the profile (only Houston present), declined to change the address without details, and explained they couldn’t add a new product (laptop) to the pending order given tool constraints. They proposed permissible changes and summarized them. Before making any write, the agent requested explicit confirmation to modify the wristwatch to black dial with leather strap. After user confirmation, they used product details to select the correct variant and executed the change via the modify tool. The final message accurately reflected the updated order and refund details ($77.15) to the gift card, and confirmed the address remained unchanged. No unsupported claims, no unauthorized actions, and proper confirmation before changes. Therefore the interaction meets the policy and pass bar.
